question: How much will a sum of ₹72,000 become after one year if the interest is compounded half-yearly at 10% per annum compound interest?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For **half-yearly compounding**, the rate becomes half (5%) and time periods double (2 periods).

Effective interest rate for 2 periods at 5% = 5 + 5 + (5 × 5)/100 = **10.25%**.

Total Amount = 110.25% of **₹72,000**.

⇒ Amount = 72,000 × 1.1025 = **₹79,380**.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹79,380.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Principal (P) = ₹72,000, Rate (R) = 10% p.a., Time (T) = 1 year.

**Formula Used:** Amount (A) = P(1 + r/100)ⁿ

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/03c39358d5f7d9f7f59e19c800628fb17a4b979a8fea5865dc2195fe045ca6c2.png] 

Since the interest is compounded **half-yearly**:

⇒ New Rate (r) = 10% ÷ 2 = **5% per half-year**.

⇒ Total periods (n) = 1 year × 2 = **2 half-years**.

⇒ A = 72,000 × (1 + 5/100)²

⇒ A = 72,000 × (105/100) × (105/100)

⇒ A = 72,000 × (21/20) × (21/20)

⇒ A = (72,000 ÷ 400) × 441

⇒ A = 180 × 441

⇒ A = ₹79,380

**∴ The correct answer is ₹79,380.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Compounding Frequency Rules

For **Half-yearly** compounding, Rate = R/2 and Time = 2T. For **Quarterly** compounding, Rate = R/4 and Time = 4T.

Effective Rate Formula

Effective Rate for 2 periods = x + y + (xy/100)%, where x and y are the rates for each period.

CI vs SI Difference

The difference between CI and SI for 2 years (or 2 periods) is given by D = P(r/100)².
